newsitem.title: BARBADOS: Clinton raises case of jailed U.S. couple.
newsitem.headline: Clinton raises case of jailed U.S. couple.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton on Saturday told the prime minister of St. Vincent he wanted a U.S. couple imprisoned on the island on murder charges to receive due process under the law, a U.S. official said.
U.S. citizens James and Penny Fletcher, of Huntingdon, West Virginia, were arrested on the Caribbean island last October, imprisoned and charged with the murder of a water taxi driver.
The report suggested there was little evidence that the two committed the murder other than the fact they were apparently the last to see the driver alive.
In Barbados for a summit with leaders from the Caribbean, Clinton raised the issue with the St. Vincent prime minister, James F. Mitchell.

"The president did have an opportunity to discuss the Fletcher case with the prime minister and indicated his concern and his hope that at the highest level there would be an effort to make sure that full due process was given to the case," U.S. deputy national security adviser Jim Steinberg told reporters.
He declined to give further details on the matter, which has already been taken up with the St. Vincent government by other U.S. officials.
